turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why does my son's gradebook show a zero, and why did I hear about it from Owen and not from you?
Sorry, I'm a bit frazzled, it's report card week.
That's not Owen's problem. The zero went in on November 3 and nobody called me, so who decided it, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
You're the first parent this month who's actually listened to me. Thank you. I mean it.
Don't manage me, Hale. I haven't said anything worth thanking me for, and you haven't answered me yet.
I really needed that today. Can we just be kind to each other in here?
I'm here about my son, not about being kind to each other. You asked for this meeting, so tell me what you have on Owen's essay.
